footer.tagline: Bringing Italy's mountain villages online — discover, explore and help them thrive.

home.heroIntro: Empowering mountain villages through digital visibility and sustainable travel. Explore authentic Italian villages, access clear and updated information, and travel beyond the usual routes — while helping local communities thrive.
home.aboutLead: A single home for Italy's mountain heritage.
home.aboutBody: Mountain-Able is a shared platform where small Italian municipalities publish and keep up to date the tourism information of their villages — attractions, events, traditions and practical details — and where travellers discover places that rarely appear on the usual maps. By centralising trustworthy information and community reviews, we help underrepresented villages gain visibility while giving visitors a richer, more responsible way to explore.
home.aboutBody2: Every visit to a mountain village supports local families, artisans and traditions. We surface the events, food and crafts that keep these communities alive, so your journey directly benefits the places you discover — not just the crowded destinations everyone already knows.
home.routeLead: Half the challenge of a mountain village is reaching it.
home.routeBody: Winding roads, steep climbs and long distances put many travellers off before they start. Our journey planner maps the route to any village, shows the terrain and elevation you'll climb, and points out the fuel, food, water and viewpoints along the way — so you can plan the drive, not just the destination.

routePoint.terrain: See the climb before you drive it — full elevation profile, total ascent and the steepest sections.
routePoint.services: Know where the fuel, food, water and rest stops are along a road that may have few.
routePoint.discover: Discover other villages you'll pass close to, and turn one trip into several.

faq.a1: Mountain-Able is a digital platform that gathers tourism information about small Italian mountain villages in one place. Municipalities publish and maintain their village pages, and travellers can search, discover and review these often-overlooked destinations.
faq.a2: Villages are managed by municipality officers — official representatives of each comune. Officers request an account, an administrator approves it, and they can then create and update the villages belonging to their municipality. Tourists cannot create villages, only review them.
faq.a3: Yes. Browsing villages, reading and writing reviews, and creating a tourist account are completely free. The platform exists to promote mountain communities, not to sell bookings.
faq.a4: Every registered tourist can leave one review with a 1–5 star rating per village. A village's average score and review count are recalculated automatically from all approved reviews, so the rating always reflects genuine visitor feedback.
faq.q5: How do I report incorrect information?
faq.a5: Use the Support link in the footer to contact us, or report a specific review for moderation. Administrators review reported content and can correct or remove inaccurate information.

about.title: About Mountain-Able
about.lead: A digital bridge for Italy's mountain communities.
about.missionBody: Italy's mountain villages hold centuries of culture, craft and natural beauty, yet many struggle with depopulation and low visibility. Mountain-Able gives every small municipality a single, trustworthy place to tell its story, and gives travellers an easy way to find and support these communities.
about.whatWeDoBody: We centralise tourism information, make villages discoverable through search and maps, and let visitors share honest reviews. Municipality officers keep each page accurate, while administrators safeguard the quality of the content.
about.scopeBody: The platform focuses on discovery and information — not bookings, payments or transport. This keeps it a neutral, community-first showcase for mountain heritage.

coord.pageIntro: Your village cannot offer everything a visitor needs, but the valley usually can. Declare what your municipality is able to provide, see what your neighbours offer, and ask when you need something you do not have.

response.offerHint: You can provide what was asked for.
response.partialHint: You can cover some of it — one vehicle instead of two, one day instead of both.
response.declineHint: Useful to say so: silence looks the same as not having read it.

cap.intro: Declare what your municipality can offer a neighbouring comune. Nothing here is published to visitors — this directory is read by other administrations only.
cap.editHint: What exactly you can offer, and who a neighbour should contact. The arrangement itself happens between the two administrations, off the platform.
cap.detailPlaceholder: Nine-seat minibus, weekdays only, outside school-transport hours.

neighbours.intro: Municipalities near you, ranked by real travel time rather than distance — across a ridge, ten kilometres can be an hour. Browse freely; you do not need to raise a request to see who offers what.
neighbours.noneHint: No municipality within {{radius}} km has declared this service.
neighbours.nearestHint: Outside the radius you chose. Shown so you can decide, rather than the search quietly widening itself.

outgoing.intro: Requests your municipality has raised, and what came back.
outgoing.raiseHint: Describe what you need. We will show you exactly which municipalities it goes to before anything is sent.

outgoing.titlePlaceholder: Transport for 40 walkers from the valley floor
outgoing.detailsPlaceholder: Dates, numbers, and anything a neighbour would need to know to answer.

outgoing.emptyHint: When your municipality cannot provide something a visitor needs, ask the valley.
outgoing.closeHint: Only you can say whether the need was met. An offer is not the same as the problem being solved.
outgoing.notePlaceholder: How it was resolved, or why it could not be.
outgoing.noteWhy: Kept as the record. Unmet requests are what tell a regional authority which services are missing from this territory.

incoming.intro: Requests from neighbouring municipalities. Answering costs little, and a clear no is more useful than silence.
incoming.emptyHint: Requests addressed to your municipality appear here.
incoming.messagePlaceholder: What you can do, and any conditions.
incoming.contactHint: The platform introduces you and stops there — you and the other comune arrange the rest directly, as you would today.

authority.intro: Every request records what was sought, where, and whether it was met. Pooled across the territory, that becomes evidence of which capabilities are persistently absent — something no single municipality can produce alone.
authority.gapsHint: A service nobody offers and nobody asks for is not a gap. One asked for repeatedly and offered by nobody is.
authority.demandHint: What the territory asked for, and how much of it went unanswered.
authority.coverageHint: Which services are declared where. An empty cell is the finding: no municipality in that region offers it at all.
authority.engagementHint: Distinguishes two things the demand table cannot: a capability that does not exist, and neighbours who are not engaging. They call for opposite responses.
authority.isolationHint: Municipalities with no neighbour nearby offering anything. For these, the answer is provision rather than introduction.
authority.noneIsolated: Every municipality has at least one neighbour offering something.
authority.noRequestsHint: Evidence accumulates as municipalities begin to ask each other.
authority.smallNumbers: Rates are withheld where fewer than {{n}} requests have been decided: a percentage from one or two cases would be a lie told with a true number. Counts are always shown.

admin.intro: The shared vocabulary for inter-municipal coordination. A fixed list is what lets declarations and requests be aggregated across the territory; free text cannot be.
admin.deleteConfirm: Delete “{{name}}”? If any municipality has declared it or any request references it, deletion is refused — retire it instead.
